back: Taylor's approach: study work scientifically to find the one best way, specialise tasks and pay for output.
Timing each movement in a task to remove waste and set a standard time and output.
Pay for each unit produced: motivates speed but may harm quality and gives no pay when production stops.
Mayo's approach: workers are motivated by social needs, attention and group belonging as well as pay.
Mayo's experiments in the 1920s and 1930s: output rose when workers were given attention, even when conditions worsened (the Hawthorne effect).
Strengths: higher output, clear standards. Weaknesses: boredom, quality problems, assumes money is the only motivator.
Strengths: better morale, lower turnover. Weaknesses: slow and costly; happy workers are not always productive.
Taylor: economic view, pay, managers plan, specialised individual tasks. Mayo: social view, belonging, consultation, teams.
Weekly pay = units produced x rate per unit. Standard output = (60 / minutes per unit) x hours x days.
